zkFL: the aggregator proves in Halo2, over Pedersen commitments, that it aggregated the clients' committed updates; clients verify (a blockchain variant hands verification to miners); proof generation up to about 54.7 min (ResNet50), verification about half of that; client encryption 10-45 min (ResNet18-34); on-chain cost analysed, not measured. Who checks: FL clients. Coded 10 Nov.

largest_model: LeNet (T-Less case study); gradient vectors in the cost tests
notes: EV-FL: the cloud server proves its weighted aggregation on challenged gradients with a zk-SNARK (jsnark); IIoT devices verify; device preparation nearly constant in clients and gradients; server aggregation slower than VerifyNet and VeriFL, verification slightly faster than VeriFL; less device energy (Raspberry Pi with a power meter); LeNet about 98% on T-Less. Who checks: FL clients. Coded 10 Nov.

PHV-FL: Groth16 (circom/snarkjs) proves that personalised models are weighted sums of edge models; verification about 8-9 ms, nearly constant with model size (Table 2); mAP@0.5 0.24; no proving time reported. Who checks: FL clients. Coded 10 Nov.

PVFL: linearly homomorphic hash (NIST P-256) lets clients check the server's aggregate; communication and computation for verification independent of dropouts (Tables IV-IX); accuracy vs NbAFL. Who checks: FL clients. Coded 10 Nov.
SVHFL: aggregation commitments; mutual verification (server screens malformed updates, clients check the aggregate). Who checks: FL clients. Coded 10 Nov.
PPVerifier: Paillier encryption and hashes let participants check the cloud's aggregation; additive secret sharing against collusion. Who checks: FL clients. Coded 10 Nov.

PrVFL: linearly homomorphic hash + hash commitments verify the aggregate; Bulletproofs range proofs verify the server's pruning. Who checks: FL clients. Coded 10 Nov.
